questions.question: Which best describes the original Mitchell et al. (2019) Model Card?
options: An electronics-datasheet-style document covering motivation, composition, collection process, labeling, uses, distribution, and maintenance
A modular, three-zoom-level document -- telescopic, periscopic, microscopic -- designed as a boundary object for different kinds of readers
A 'nutrition label' for ML models, covering training data, intended use, factors, metrics, evaluation data, disaggregated analyses, ethical considerations, and caveats
An end-to-end system document covering security capabilities, prompt-injection protection, data-exfiltration detection, and incident response
questions.explanation: The lesson describes the Mitchell et al. 2019 Model Card as a 'nutrition label' for models, covering training data, intended use, factors, metrics, evaluation data, quantitative disaggregated analyses, ethical considerations, and caveats -- the datasheet, data-card, and system-card descriptions are separate documentation formats.

questions.question: What did Oreamuno et al. (2023) find about ethical-considerations adoption in Hugging Face model cards?
options: Approximately 0.3% of Hugging Face model cards document ethical considerations -- the adoption gap the lesson calls the documentation problem
Approximately 80% of Hugging Face model cards document ethical considerations, since most maintainers copy the standard Mitchell 2019 template
No Hugging Face model card contains any text at all, since the platform only stores structured metadata fields, not free text
All Hugging Face model cards document ethical considerations, because the platform enforces the field as mandatory before upload
questions.explanation: The lesson cites Oreamuno et al. 2023's audit finding that only about 0.3% of Hugging Face model cards document ethical considerations, illustrating the adoption gap the lesson calls the documentation problem -- not 80%, not zero text, and not a mandatory field.

questions.question: What does Pushkarna et al. (Google 2022) Data Cards' telescopic / periscopic / microscopic layering provide?
options: A pre-RLHF audit checklist used to verify that a base model's training data was collected under an approved data-governance policy
A telescope-themed visualization library for plotting per-layer attention weights and gradient norms across a transformer's full depth
A privacy-preserving query interface that lets auditors run statistical queries over a dataset without ever viewing raw records
A boundary-object framing where the same document serves non-experts, ML practitioners, and auditors via three zoom levels of detail
questions.explanation: The lesson describes Data Cards' three zoom levels -- telescopic (non-expert summary), periscopic (ML-practitioner overview), and microscopic (auditor-level detail) -- as a boundary-object design where the same document serves different readers, not an audit checklist, a visualization tool, or a query interface.

questions.question: What scope does a System Card cover that Model Cards do not?
options: Only the dataset used to train the model, documented the same way a Datasheet covers motivation, composition, and collection process
End-to-end AI system scope: model, safety stack, and deployment context, covering security, prompt-injection protection, and incident response
Only the prompt template and few-shot examples baked into the system prompt, without any coverage of the surrounding deployment stack
Only the tokenizer's vocabulary and merge rules, independent of how the model is actually deployed or safeguarded in production
questions.explanation: The lesson scopes System Cards to the end-to-end AI system -- model plus safety stack plus deployment context -- covering security capabilities, prompt-injection protection, data-exfiltration detection, alignment with stated values, and incident response, well beyond a dataset, a prompt template, or a tokenizer.

questions.question: What did Liang et al. (2024) report about model-card detail and Hugging Face download rate?
options: Detailed model cards correlate with up to a 29% higher download rate on Hugging Face -- documentation quality is now market-driven, not only compliance-driven
Only the ethical-considerations section of a card affected downloads; other sections like training data and metrics had no measurable effect
Model-card detail had no statistically measurable effect on Hugging Face download rates anywhere in Liang et al.'s 2024 analysis
More detailed model cards actually correlate with lower download rates, since users interpret extensive documentation as a sign of a complicated model
questions.explanation: The lesson reports that Liang et al. 2024 found detailed model cards correlate with up to a 29% higher download rate on Hugging Face, framing this as evidence that adoption pressure for good documentation is now market-driven, not only compliance-driven -- not isolated to one section, not null, and not inverted.

questions.question: What does Laminator (Duddu et al. 2024) contribute to documentation?
options: An automated benchmarking harness that runs a model against standardized evaluation suites and writes the scores into its card
A full replacement for the Datasheets-for-Datasets standard, consolidating dataset and model documentation into one format
An LLM-based summary generator that drafts card text automatically from a model's training logs and configuration files
Verifiable attestations via hardware TEE and cryptographic signatures, so a card can carry a proof-of-claim rather than just an unverified claim
questions.explanation: The lesson describes Laminator (Duddu et al. 2024) as contributing verifiable attestations via hardware TEE and cryptographic signatures, so a model card can carry a proof-of-claim rather than just an unverified claim -- not a benchmarking harness, a Datasheets replacement, or a summary generator.
